subject: Realtime output freeze impacting OmniHealth integration — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Alice Li <alice@omnihealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@omnihealth.ai
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Live integration: repeated output pauses during peak window

Hi Marissa,

We started hitting intermittent pauses in the live inference stream this morning around 08:45 PDT. Client sessions see the socket remain open but no tokens are delivered for 8–20s before traffic resumes. This is causing our downstream message processor to queue up and occasionally throw a 504.

Quick details:
- Impact: ~12% of requests in the 08:45–09:30 window experienced at least one freeze
- We see higher error rate on fanout endpoints that use WebSocket chunked transfers
- Attached a small pcap and a filtered log (omnihealth_ws_log_1003.zip)

Can we get someone from eng to take a look? Our ops team is ready to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Li
Head of Platform, OmniHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Li <alice@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jon as Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live integration: repeated output pauses during peak window

Thanks Alice — sorry for the interruption. Looping in Dev (oncall) and Laura (CS lead).

Dev / Laura — attaching Alice's logs. Can you confirm whether this matches the brief downtime pattern we saw in the fleet at 08:45? If this needs exec attention I will escalate immediately.

Next steps I suggest:
- Dev: triage pcap + streaming logs and flag whether this is a client-side backpressure or server-side stall
- Laura: coordinate a 30-minute war room with OmniHealth ops, provide a short customer-facing note

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alice Li <alice@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live integration: repeated output pauses during peak window

On Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 9:28 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Alice — sorry for the interruption. Looping in Dev (oncall) and Laura (CS lead).

Thanks Marissa / Alice. I pulled the snippets — initial hypothesis: intermittent long-tail stalls in the token pump that correlate with high-concurrency prefix cache eviction. Symptoms I see in the logs:
- Server keeps the WebSocket open; no TCP resets observed in the pcap
- Token emission halts for 6–18s, then a burst of 30–200 tokens comes through
- We have a few entries in runtime indicating a fallback to CP:evict and a queued batch spike

I want to escalate to infra quickly: looping in Jonas and Rishi for visibility. We can try a temporary mitigation (lower concurrency for OmniHealth routing, enable aggressive KV pinning for their trial flow) while we root-cause.

I'll prepare a short mitigation plan in the next 30m.

—Dev
Dev Patel | Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Alice Li <alice@omnihealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live integration: repeated output pauses during peak window

Thanks Dev — please include the metrics showing latency distribution and per-tenant parallelism. This looks like a potential unit-economics/availability vector that should surface to the exec team given OmniHealth's scale.

Immediate asks:
- Dev: post the query results for 1h and 5m P50/P95/P99 token latency and active connections for OmniHealth
- Rishi: can you confirm whether any recent kernel/quantization rollout touched the real-time path in the last 48h?
- Marissa / Laura: schedule a 11:00 call with Omni ops (30m war room) and prep a one-slide status note for leadership.

I will join the call. If the mitigation (lower concurrency / pinning) is safe, prioritize that while we gather traces.

Jonas Weber | VP, Customer Reliability
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Alice Li <alice@omnihealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live integration: repeated output pauses during peak window

On Fri, Oct 3, 2025 at 10:05 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Dev — please include the metrics showing latency distribution and per-tenant parallelism.

Checked the rollout logs — no model quantization or kernel changes deployed to the real-time fleet in the last 72h. However, there was an autoscaler config tweak that altered kube pod eviction thresholds on 2025-10-02 23:10 UTC. That change can increase batch coalescing under high load and looks suspicious with the observed spike pattern.

I recommend two actions now:
1) Roll back the eviction threshold tweak in the us-west cluster for the next 2h and monitor
2) Apply a conservative concurrency cap specifically for OmniHealth routing (reduce max inflight to 12)

If both are safe we should see a reduction in the long-tail stalls.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Director, Inference Ops
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Li <alice@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Oct 2025 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live integration: repeated output pauses during peak window

Alice — we scheduled a short war room for 11:00 PDT. Status update:
- Engineering suspects an autoscaler eviction threshold change introduced unusual batch growth under peak concurrency; we are rolling that config back in us-west and applying a temporary concurrency cap for your tenant.
- You may see a small drop in throughput as we cap inflight requests; this is to avoid the long tail freezes.
- Attached is a quick FAQ for your ops team and the metrics CSV showing the hit rate.

We appreciate the quick reporting and will follow up with a post-mortem.

Marissa
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Li <alice@omnihealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 5 Oct 2025 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident exec brief: OmniHealth realtime freezes (Oct 3)

Alice, team —

Thank you for your patience while we investigated. Summary for leadership:
- Incident window: Oct 3, 2025 08:45–10:20 PDT
- Root cause: aggressive pod eviction thresholds combined with high prefix cache churn caused transient batch coalescing spikes in the real-time pipeline, which manifested as multi-second token emission freezes on open WebSocket connections.
- Customer impact: elevated error rate and latency for ~12% of requests during the window; a small portion of sessions hit downstream 504s.
- Mitigation applied: rolled back eviction tweak in us-west, enabled tenant-level concurrency cap, and pinned critical prefix entries for OmniHealth. Immediate mitigation reduced observed freezes to <1% in follow-up monitoring.

Next steps (post-mortem actions):
- Engineering: add circuit-breaker telemetry for per-tenant batch size and token emission gaps (owner: Dev)
- Infra: revert autoscaler config change to staged rollout and add canary tests for real-time path (owner: Rishi)
- CS/AE: provide a formal SLA credit calculation within 48h (owner: Laura / Marissa)

I've filed the internal incident ticket: INF-2894 (link above). We will share the post-mortem document by Wednesday. If you would like a call with execs to review impact and credits, let us know and we will arrange.

Respectfully,
Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: omnihealth_ws_log_1003.zip, pcap-snippet-1003.txt, SLA-impact-metrics.csv
